stemBlocks.value: Mr. Lee invested $40 000 at 7% per annum compound interest for 2 years. Calculate the value of the investment at the end of each year.
Think first: The question wants both year-end values, so work year by year rather than jumping to the final amount.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p018-q09 from workbook page 18.

solutionSteps.instruction: Turn the rate into a multiplier.
Find the value at the end of year 1.
Apply the multiplier to the new balance.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply by 1.07 to get the value after one year, then multiply that result by 1.07 again.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: End of year 1: $42 800.  End of year 2: $45 796.

whyThisWorks.value: Compound interest is charged on the balance at the start of each year, so the second year's 7% is taken on $42 800 rather than on the original $40 000. That is why the year-two interest of $2 996 exceeds the year-one interest of $2 800 — the extra $196 is 7% of the first year's interest.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding $2 800 twice, which is simple interest and gives $45 600.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding $2 800 twice, which is simple interest and gives $45 600.
Avoid this: Multiplying $40 000 by 1.14 instead of 1.07².
